text.p: More Group Plc , Britain's largest outdoor advertising company, is moving aggressively to expand in the U.S., which offers the company its greatest growth prospects, chief executive Roger Parry said.
"The U.S. represents our greatest growth opportunity," Parry told Reuters in an interview on Friday ahead of the company's release of 1996 results on March 6.
"Our second greatest growth opportunity is Asia," he said.
More Group, which commands 19 percent of the British outdoor ad market, last October bought a small New York-based street furniture advertising firm as a vehicle for expansion into the U.S.
Street furniture includes bus and tram shelters, newsstands, bicycle racks and recycling bins, with bus shelters the largest component of the sector.

The U.S., the world's largest outdoor advertising market, is currently dominated by billboards. More Group, however, is seeking to expand its street furniture business into the U.S., a relatively untapped business in America.

More Group is currently on a shortlist of candidates for a street furniture contract in Westchester County, a suburban area north of New York, and is also plans to bid on a large street furniture contract in New York City.
New York City represents the world's largest outdoor advertising market, with 3,500 bus shelters and 4,000 newsstands at stake in the contract up for bid.

Winning the 20-year, New York City contract could require an investment of $75 million to $100 million, Parry said. If More Group were to win the contract, the venture could become cashflow positive "within a few years," he said.
But even if More is not successful in New York, it sees ample opportunity in America.

The company is at the final stages of negotiating a street furniture contract in St. Louis, and is in talks for similar contacts in Denver, Boston and Chicago. Parry noted that many U.S. cities are so large they exceed the total populations of some European countries -- and the U.S. bus shelter market remains virtually untapped.
"In Britain we operate approximately 30,000 bus shelter panels," he said. "In the totality of the U.S. there are only about 30,000 bus shelter panels."
Because bus shelter advertising remains a fledgling market in the U.S., Parry said his company does "...have to sort of preach the gospel of street furniture."

Advertising on bus shelters already exists in New York, but the space typically is sold on a longterm basis to local advertisers. More, on the other hand, in its European markets sells bus shelter space on a short-term basis to large advertisers -- the same kind of advertisers who hawk their wares on television.

In Britain bus shelter space is sold in two-week blocks, compared to one week in France and 10 days in Scandanavia. More Group expects that in the U.S. it would initially sell space in four-week blocks, later reducing the selling period to two weeks.
"Advertising research shows that after about two weeks you tend to get a high level of repeat viewing," Parry said. "So the advertising impact is less valuable."

More Group is also on a short list of candidates for a bus shelter contract in Oslo, a particularly attractive opportunity because the contract represents the introduction of the medium into Norway, Parry said.

Although the Asian outdoor advertising market is growing rapidly, More Group's own growth prospects are more limited there. "A lot of the growth in Asia will be unavailable to us because it will be small, local businesses," Parry said.

More Group, on the other hand, is just coming out of a period of restructuring in France. The company's 1996 results will include "a fairly major provision" on the French restructuring, Parry said. The overall French outdoor market grew about five percent in 1996, the first time in years that the market experienced growth.

As More Group moves forward with expansion opportunties, Parry said the growth will come from organic growth rather than major acquisitions. The company could pursue small acquisitions in the U.S., he said, but added, "I think it's unlikely we would make any major acquisitions in the U.S."
